content: 1. Zhao F. published a study in 2021 titled Synonymous but not Silent: The Codon Usage Code for Gene Expression and Protein Folding, which appeared in the Annual Review of Biochemistry (Volume 90, pages 375–401). This work explores how synonymous codon substitutions influence gene expression and protein folding. 2. Rodriguez A., Wright GS, Lundgren TJ, Moss MJ, Li J, Milenkovic T, and colleagues demonstrated in a 2022 bioRxiv study that synonymous codon substitutions can regulate transcription and translation of upstream genes (DOI: 10.1101/2022.05.29.502938). 3. Hegelmeyer NK, Previti ML, Andrade J, Utama R, Sejour RJ, Gardin J, and others reported in 2023 on how gene recoding through synonymous mutations leads to promiscuous intragenic transcription initiation in mycobacteria, as published on bioRxiv (DOI: 10.1101/2023.05.26.53260). 4. Yadon AN, Maharaj K, Adamson JH, Lai YP, Sacchettini JC, Ioerger TR, and colleagues conducted a comprehensive characterization of PncA polymorphisms that confer resistance to pyrazinamide in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Nature Communications in 2017 (Volume 8, Article 588). 5. Omar SV, Hillemann D, Pandey S, Merker M, Witt AK, Nadarajan D, and others highlighted systematic errors in rifampicin resistance detection using the Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra assay. Their findings, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2020 (Volume 24, Issue 12, pages 1307–1311), have implications for the regulation of genotypic assays. 6. Ocheretina O, Brandao AP, Pang Y, Rodrigues C, Banu S, Ssengooba W, and colleagues investigated the impact of bacillary load on the accuracy of rifampicin resistance results using the Xpert® MTB/RIF assay. Their study appeared in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2021 (Volume 25, Issue 11, pages 881–885). 7. Rigouts L, Keyser J, Rabab R, Fissette K, van Deun A, de Jong BC, and others evaluated the performance of the GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay in detecting uncommon rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in BMC Research Notes in 2023 (Volume 16, Article 146). 8. Blakemore R and Alland D addressed diagnostic inconsistencies observed with an obsolete version of the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, noting that such issues are unlikely to recur with the current version. This was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2014 (Volume 52, Issue 2, page 704). 9. Hunt M, Letcher B, Malone KM, Nguyen G, Hall MB, Colquhoun RM, and others developed Minos, a tool for variant adjudication and joint genotyping of bacterial genome cohorts. Their work appeared in Genome Biology in 2022 (Volume 23, Article 147). 10. Rausch T, Zichner T, Schlattl A, Stütz AM, Benes V, and Korbel JO introduced DELLY, a method for structural variant discovery using integrated paired-end and split-read analysis. This was published in Bioinformatics in 2012 (Volume 28, Issue 18, pages i333–i339). 11. The Seq&Treat initiative focuses on next-generation tuberculosis care, providing resources for sequencing and treatment strategies (available at next-generationtbcare.org/tb/seq-treat). 12. The WHO technical manual for drug susceptibility testing of tuberculosis medicines provides guidelines for evaluating resistance to TB treatments (available at int/iris/handle/10665/275469). 13. Martin L, Coronel J, Faulx D, Valdez M, Metzler M, Crudder C, and others conducted a field evaluation of the Hardy TB MODS Kit™ for rapid phenotypic diagnosis of tuberculosis and multidrug-resistant TB. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2014 (Volume 9, Issue 9, Article e107258). 14. Guidelines for drug susceptibility testing of second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs for DOTS-Plus programs are available through the WHO (int/iris/handle/10665/83807). 15. The WHO companion handbook for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis provides detailed guidance for implementing treatment strategies (int/iris/handle/10665/130918). 16. Torre A, Ng KCS, Van Deun A, André E, Kaisergruber J, Ssengooba W, and others examined the variable ability of rapid tests to detect rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that confer phenotypically occult rifampicin resistance. Their study was published in Scientific Reports in 2019 (Volume 9, Article 11826). 17. Verboven L, Phelan J, Heupink TH, and Van Rie A developed TBProfiler, an automated tool for associating genetic variants in Mycobacterium tuberculosis with drug resistance. This was published in PLoS One in 2022 (Volume 17, Issue 12, Article e0279644). 18. Zhang Y, Dhandayuthapani S, and Deretic V elucidated the molecular basis for the sensitivity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to isoniazid. Their findings were published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA in 1996 (Volume 93, Issue 23, pages 13212–13216). 19. Hicks ND, Giffen SR, Culviner PH, Chao MC, Dulberger CL, Liu Q, and others identified mutations in dnaA and cryptic interaction sites that increase drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study appeared in PLoS Pathogens in 2020 (Volume 16, Issue 11, Article e1009063). 20. Vilchèze C, Av-Gay Y, Attarian R, Liu Z, Hazbón M, Colangeli R, and others demonstrated that mycothiol biosynthesis is essential for ethionamide susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their work was published in Molecular Microbiology in 2008 (Volume 69, Issue 5, pages 1316–1329).
